description: Paging vectors for the SentiLab view, DRAFT v0.6 (view-envelope-0.6.md, rule 4). Generated by `node run-paging-vectors.mjs --write` and checked by `node run-paging-vectors.mjs`. Envelopes keep v0.5's format; the V1 rows come from ../view-envelope-v0.5/vectors-view.json. Scenarios give the polls, what the server does at each, hand-written expectations and the full trace.

rules.cursor_hash: lowercase hex SHA-256 over the raw bytes of rows 0..n-1, each followed by one LF; computed on bytes as received, never on decoded text
rules.request: { cursor, limit } plus cursor_hash for every cursor above 0; never a seq parameter
rules.ok: status 200, body within 256 lines and 4 MiB, x-next-cursor a decimal integer equal to cursor + rows returned, and x-cursor-hash equal to the client's own hash of all rows it would then hold
rules.failures: transport: no response, a status other than 200, 400, 404, 409 or 501, or a body over the caps; paging_error: a bad x-next-cursor or x-cursor-hash; stream_replaced: 409; paging_unsupported: 400, 404 or 501. A failed poll keeps no rows and never resets the cursor; stream_replaced and paging_unsupported stay until a manual reload
rules.label: a failed latest poll shows "STALE · <reason>" (transport, paging error, stream replaced, paging unsupported); otherwise, if K is below the highest value it has reached, "STALE · chain broken" at once; otherwise the v0.5 progress tracker, fed only with valid pages, gives LIVE or STALE
rules.bytes_to_rows: split raw bytes on LF (0x0A) only; a trailing LF doesn't start a row; decode each row on its own as strict UTF-8 keeping any BOM (TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true })); a row that isn't valid UTF-8 is malformed (invalid_utf8), a row starting with a BOM is malformed (not_json, since JSON.parse rejects it), and the page continues; the same for replay files; the hash never sees decoded text
rules.server: 400 for a cursor or limit outside the allowed range; 409 for a cursor beyond the end, or above 0 without a cursor_hash or with one that doesn't match; otherwise up to `limit` rows within 4 MiB, with x-next-cursor, x-has-more and x-cursor-hash
rules.rows: text rows are UTF-8; base64 rows are raw bytes; fill rows are `bytes` copies of `fill`. In logs and bodies, ["id", n] means n copies
rules.server_behaviors: log: servePage() over that log; headers: overrides, null removes; tamper: replace that log row in the body only; page: exactly those rows after the log, consistent headers, no limit; status + legacy: that status for cursor requests, and a legacy 200 page (rows with seq > after, no paging headers) if a request carries after; network_error: no response

bytes_to_rows.name: a trailing LF ends the last row and doesn't start a new one
no trailing LF: the last row is still a row
a blank line in the middle is a row
an empty body has no rows
a lone LF is one blank row
only LF splits: a CR stays in the row
invalid UTF-8 (FF) is no text, and the next row still decodes
an overlong encoding (C0 AF) is not valid UTF-8
an encoded surrogate (ED A0 80) is not valid UTF-8

cursor_hash_cases.name: no rows: the SHA-256 of nothing
one row {}: the SHA-256 of {} and LF
a row with invalid UTF-8 is hashed as received; decoding first would give a different hash

server_logs.log600: row i (0 to 599) is the ASCII text {"row":i}, except when i % 100 is 7: then it is {"row":i,"raw":" followed by the bytes FF FE and then "}

server_cases.name: cursor 256 with the hash of rows 0..255: rows 256 to 511
cursor 512: the last 88 rows, no more
a stale cursor_hash (from a log whose row 3 differs): 409
rows of 65,535 bytes: a page stops at 64 rows, exactly 4 MiB

scenarios.name: C2 truncated log: the log shrinks to 5 rows, so cursor 11 is beyond its end; 409, stream replaced, the prefix is kept and the client doesn't reset
C3 bad x-next-cursor: missing, not an integer (eleven, 11.0), backwards (7), and not n plus the rows (12); each is a paging error and the prefix is kept
C4 rows, not envelopes: a byte-identical duplicate, a non-JSON row and a row with invalid UTF-8 each advance the cursor by one; the result equals verifying the same rows as one file

scenarios.name: C6a no cursor support from the start (404; the server would answer after=<seq>): STALE · paging unsupported for 70 s, never LIVE, no seq paging
C6b cursor support lost (501) after seq 1..8 were paged: the prefix is kept, STALE · paging unsupported, never LIVE again
C6c a 400 on the cursor parameters is no cursor support too
C8a replaced log of the same length (row 5 differs): the old cursor_hash gets 409, stream replaced, the prefix is kept, no reset
C8b replaced log that is longer (row 5 differs, two rows added): the old cursor_hash gets 409, stream replaced, the prefix is kept
C9 hash mismatch: a page whose row 9 was altered in transit, then a page with no x-cursor-hash; each is a paging error and its rows are not kept
C10 bytes to rows: one page holding a BOM-prefixed copy of seq 1 and a row of invalid UTF-8; both are malformed, the 11 other rows verify, and the cursor hash covers the raw bytes of all 13
